messages:
Sam: FYI opening an escalation about customer-reported SSE disconnects. Mobile app users see partial chunks then stream just drops; they reconnect once and sometimes get duplicate fragments. Customer on hosted (eu-west-1). Repro steps + logs below.

Maya: thanks — can you paste repro steps & trace ids?

Sam: Repro steps: 1) POST /v1/chat/stream with model=redwood-7b and small prompt (~50 tokens) 2) Client uses EventSource 3) After ~18–40s we see some partial 'data:' events then nothing, no 'event: done' 4) Client 'onerror' triggers and it reconnects once (exp backoff) Observed root response headers: ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
cache-control: no-cache
connection: keep-alive
transfer-encoding: chunked``` Server debug id: rwd-ctl-01 / trace=trc_2026_03_08_582

Eli: are we seeing 502/504 or an LB FIN? Any proxy logs?

Sam: No 502/504. Connection logs show socket FIN from our LB for some sessions. LB idle timeout currently 30s. Mobile client set to wait longer which leads to truncated sequences on their side.

Jin: this points at idle timeouts in intermediaries. Two mitigation axes: (A) application-level heartbeats (SSE comment pings or small data events) and (B) OS/TCP keepalive and LB tuning. Also check client reconnect + dedupe semantics.

Maya: proposed mitigation draft: - Server: send SSE comment ping `: hb\n\n` every 15s by default - LB/proxy: recommend idle timeout to 60s where possible; document constraints for Private deployments - Client: reconnect with jittered backoff and dedupe via `X-Stream-Id` header to avoid duplicate tokens - Observability: emit `sse.heartbeat.sent` counter and `sse.disconnect.cause` (idle/proxy/reset)

Sam: Support note: some customers still saw disconnects at ~5m even with comment pings — suspect some proxies strip comment lines. Fallbacks: 1) send a tiny `data` event periodically (clients should ignore empty payloads) or 2) emit `event: ping
data: {"t": <ts>}
\n` which clients can ignore and intermediaries won't strip.

Eli: careful: some clients treat empty `data:` as a message. I like structured `event: ping` so clients can ignore `ping` events explicitly. Intermediaries generally pass through event/data lines.

Jin: runtime change: if no bytes sent for ~25s and no tokens generated, proactively flush a heartbeat. If LB issues a FIN within next 5s, mark `disconnect.cause = proxy-idle` and add to infra queue.

Maya: experiment plan: run two A/B tests for 48h across hosted traffic: (A) comment ping every 15s for 10% traffic, (B) `event: ping` every 30s for 10% traffic. Measure reconnection rates, duplicate token counts, and `LB FIN` events.

Sam: Repro instructions for CS: - Use EventSource via curl: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream` and watch for abrupt drop without final event. Capture tcpdump and response headers. - Check `X-Stream-Id` and `rwd-trace` in logs to correlate. - For mobile reproduce, run a local proxy (Charles/Fiddler) to see if someone rewrites or strips `:` comments.

Eli: Ops action items: - Add `sse.heartbeat.sent` metric in runtime - Add an SSE probe that opens a stream and measures gap-to-first-byte across hops - Audit LB idle timeout and enable per-tenant keepalive options for Dedicated

Jin: Perf/cost note: heartbeats add small bytes but at scale it matters. For Dedicated expose heartbeat interval config (min 5s, default 15s).

Maya: Auth corner-case: customers using short-lived tokens (<=60s) can hit 401 on reconnect. Add docs section recommending silent token refresh and include `WWW-Authenticate` semantics.

Sam: Draft message to customer: ```Hi <cust>,
We suspect intermediate proxies are tearing down idle SSE sessions. Interim mitigation: enable server-side heartbeat pings (15s) for your tenant and, if possible, set your LB idle timeout to 60s. We'll run experiments to find the most robust ping format. Can you enable proxy logging (Charles/Android tcpdump) and confirm if you have a CDN/edge in front of our API? We'll collect 48h of logs and reassess.```

Maya: wording good. Add instructions for capturing tcpdump on Android and ask about CDN/edge.

Sam: I'll send escalation packet and opt-in heartbeat for tenant. Opening internal ticket INF-2983 for tracking.

Ops-bot: Incident created: INF-2983 (assigned: Jin, Eli) — https://tasks.redwood.ai/INF-2983

Sam: thanks all. If support surfaces other auth/billing edge-cases around disconnects, I'll add them here. Closing initial thread once customer acknowledges.
